core_obligations: Separate the listed properties into those defined globally, for which the assertion is immediate, and the local ones, which need the covering translation (proof lines 2868-2871).

For a local property, use the local character of quasi-coherence on a site to express that the associated module has the property as a condition on the members of a covering of the source (proof lines 2871-2874).
Discharge the local properties by the five earlier descent lemmas, matching each named property of the list with the corresponding lemma (proof lines 2874-2879).

Handle the exceptional case of coherence: reduce it to the finite type case through the characterisation of coherent sheaves on a locally Noetherian scheme, and note that the author marks this reduction as having omitted details (proof lines 2880-2884).
Record why locally freeness is listed as a possible exception and why the remaining cases are unaffected (statement lines 2862-2865).
proof_roadmap: Translate the local properties to a covering (proof lines 2871-2874).
Apply the five descent lemmas for the local properties (proof lines 2874-2879).
Reduce coherence to finite type, with details omitted by the author (proof lines 2880-2884).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme S, a topology among Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic and fppf, and one of the listed properties of modules -- free, finitely free, generated by global sections, generated by r global sections, generated by finitely many global sections, having a global presentation, having a global finite presentation, locally free, finite locally free, locally generated by sections, locally generated by r sections, finite type, finitely presented, coherent or flat -- the lemma asserts that a quasi-coherent module has the property if and only if its associated module on the big site or on the small site does, with a possible exception for locally free and coherent, and with the coherent case holding for the small site when S is locally Noetherian and the topology is Zariski or etale (statement lines 2829-2866). The proof divides the list in two: the properties defined globally are immediate, while for the local properties the local character of quasi-coherence on a site is used to translate the assertion into a statement on the members of a covering of the source, after which the five descent lemmas proved earlier in the chapter -- for finite type, finite presentation, locally generated by r sections, flatness and finite local freeness -- cover the list (proof lines 2868-2879). The exceptional case of coherence is then reduced to finite type using the characterisation of coherent sheaves on a locally Noetherian scheme (proof lines 2880-2884). The claim is H2: the division of fifteen named properties into the global ones and the local ones, the identification of the covering statement each local property reduces to, and the separate treatment of the two exceptions are the content of the card, and the author marks the last reduction as having omitted details, which is recorded as an obligation.
